title: K-flat Tate-unit models and uniform integral reduction domains
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum of [def-pur-conventions], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $S$. On the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], for each finite extension $L/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_L$ and uniformizer $\varpi_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], put $R_L=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,S}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and $U_L=R_L[0]$. Use the unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].
For integers $m\ge0$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$, put $J_L=\mathcal O_L(m)$, $V_L=U_L(m)$ and $W_L=V_L[n]$, with the twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. The complexes $R_L[0]$, $J_L[0]$, $(R_L\otimes_{R_L}J_L)[0]$ and their integer shifts are K-flat with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Their identity resolutions compute ordinary derived coefficient extension $C_{H/L}(K)=K\otimes^L_{R_L}R_H$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] for every finite inclusion $L\subseteq H$; the specified natural $\chi$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] identifies these computations with the strict quotient-tower extensions [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] on these complete objects, also when $H=L$.
The objects $U_L,V_L,W_L$ belong to $D^b_{ctf}(S,\mathcal O_L)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. For every $j\ge1$, their actual derived reductions [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] are canonically isomorphic in the derived category to $(\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^j)_S[0]$, $(\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^j)_S(m)[0]$ and $(\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^j)_S(m)[n]$, respectively. For every degree-zero module sheaf $M$ over $(\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^j)_S$, tensoring these reductions with $M$ gives $M[0]$, $(M\otimes(\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^j)_S(m))[0]$ and $(M\otimes(\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^j)_S(m))[n]$, respectively, in the derived category. Thus their uniform containing Tor intervals are $[0,0]$, $[0,0]$ and $[-n,-n]$, independently of $j$. These are containing intervals even for $S=\varnothing$.

proof.text: By [prop-weil-twist-preserves], $J_L$ is locally free of rank one over $R_L$. The unit is free of rank one, and multiplication $r\otimes z\mapsto rz$, inverse $z\mapsto1\otimes z$, identifies $R_L\otimes_{R_L}J_L$ with $J_L$. Apply [lem-sfb-locally-free-derived-scalars] to these three module sheaves to obtain flatness. Each displayed complex and each shift is a one-term bounded-above flat complex, so [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] gives K-flatness. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings](2), its identity resolution computes ordinary derived coefficient extension. The same calculation of the derived twist identifies $V_L$ with $J_L[0]$ and $W_L$ with $J_L[0][n]$.

proof.text: Write $A_j=(\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^j)_S$. For $U_L$, [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible](2) identifies the actual derived reduction with $A_j[0]$. For $V_L$, apply [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings](2) to the K-flat identity model of Step 1 and the actual projection $R_L\to A_j$. It yields $(J_L\otimes_{R_L}A_j)[0]$, identified with $A_j(m)[0]$ by the finite-level reduction clause of [prop-weil-twist-preserves]. The same termwise computation on the shifted identity model yields $A_j(m)[0][n]$ for $W_L$: the single nonzero term moves from degree $0$ to degree $-n$. These are isomorphisms in the finite-coefficient derived category, with the canonical K-flat comparison maps.

proof.text: The finite line $A_j(m)$ is locally free of rank one by [prop-weil-twist-preserves]. Apply [lem-sfb-locally-free-derived-scalars] to it and to $A_j$; then [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] applies to their one-term shifts as well. Compute tensor with any degree-zero $A_j$-module sheaf $M$ using these K-flat identity models, as specified in [def-weil-derived-tensor]. The total tensor has just one term: respectively $M$, $M\otimes_{A_j}A_j(m)$, and $M\otimes_{A_j}A_j(m)$ in degrees $0,0,-n$, with zero differentials. The first identification is $a\otimes x\mapsto ax$, inverse $x\mapsto1\otimes x$; exchanging the degree-zero factors gives the displayed order of the other tensors. Thus cohomology vanishes outside $[0,0]$, $[0,0]$, $[-n,-n]$, uniformly in $j$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible](2), $U_L$ is derived complete and belongs to $D^b_c(S,\mathcal O_L)$. Twisting preserves this category and derived completeness by [prop-weil-twist-preserves], so $V_L$ does too. Step 3 and the integral definition [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] place both in $D^b_{ctf}$, using the single interval $[0,0]$ for all positive reductions. Closure under shifts in [lem-weil-integral-ctf-triangulated] places $W_L$ in the same category, hence makes it derived complete; Step 3 supplies its precise containing interval $[-n,-n]$. If $S$ is empty or $M=0$, all terms vanish, so the same containing intervals still apply.

source.place: Twists preserve bounded constructibility, completeness and uniform Tor bounds; integral shift closure via lem-weil-integral-ctf-triangulated

proof.text: All the one-term objects in Step 1 and their shifts are now complete: $R_L\otimes J_L\cong J_L$, and shifts of the unit and line stay in $D^b_{ctf}$ by [lem-weil-integral-ctf-triangulated]. For each finite inclusion $L\subseteq H$, apply [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] to each such object. Its specified natural map $\chi_{H/L}$ is an isomorphism from the ordinary derived scalar extension computed in Step 1 to the strict quotient-tower scalar extension. The last clause of that node covers $H=L$: after multiplication it is the natural derived-completeness comparison. Thus the comparison used here has exactly the normalization required in the statement.
